child_profile: 2½ months old, not yet holding head up when on tummy (most babies do by 2 months).
activity_description: Carry the baby tummy-down with one hand under their tummy. Say 'Up!' as you lift them slightly, 'Down!' as you lower them, and 'All around!' as you move side to side.

child_profile: 2½ months old, not yet smiling when talked to or smiled at (most babies do by 2 months).
activity_description: Sing songs that have hand movements, such as 'Wheels on the Bus', and do the actions for the baby. Watch for smiles and movements in response.

child_profile: 2½ months old, not yet smiling when talked to or smiled at (most babies do by 2 months).
activity_description: Sit with the baby and show them photos of family members or smiling faces in a magazine. Point to each face and say who it is. Babies love faces, so keep the pictures close and give them time to look.

child_profile: 2½ months old, not yet smiling when talked to or smiled at (most babies do by 2 months).
activity_description: During daily routines, name the child's apparent emotions out loud (e.g., 'you seem happy,' 'that felt frustrating') to help them begin associating words with feelings.

child_profile: 5 months old, not yet looking at their hands with interest (most babies do by 4 months).
activity_description: While the baby lies on their back, hold a light scarf just above their chest and move it slowly. Let them swipe, bat and grab at it. Move it to different sides so they reach with both hands.

child_profile: 5 months old, not yet looking at their hands with interest (most babies do by 4 months).
activity_description: Draw the baby's attention to their feet. If they need help, give a small lift under their hips. Let them do as much as they can on their own.

child_profile: 4½ months old; the caregiver would like support with sensory development; the baby enjoys music and rattles.
activity_description: Gather the family for a few minutes of music: sing, clap, pat your knees or tap a pot with a wooden spoon while the baby watches and listens from a lap. Let the baby hold a shaker. Making music together builds closeness.

child_profile: 8 months old, not yet rolling from tummy to back (most babies do by 6 months).
activity_description: Use your hands to make shadow puppets on the wall. Talk and sing as you move your fingers while the baby watches.

child_profile: 8 months old, not yet rolling from tummy to back (most babies do by 6 months).
activity_description: Place toys in front of the baby during tummy time to encourage reaching. Try to get them to use both arms, then move the toy from side to side for more challenge.

child_profile: 11 months old, not yet smiling or laughing at peek-a-boo (most babies do by 9 months).
activity_description: Put funny hats on yourselves and look in the mirror together. Do a little dance and talk about what you are wearing.

child_profile: 16 months old, not yet stacking two small objects like blocks (most children do by 15 months).
activity_description: Fill a bucket with blocks or objects of different sizes, textures and colours, all too big to swallow. Let the child take them out, feel them and put them back. Describe each one as they explore.

child_profile: 13 months old; the caregiver would like support with sensory development; the child enjoys water play and sand.
activity_description: Fill an old bag with safe items like the ones you carry, such as an old phone, keys and family photos. Watch the child take them out and play with them just like you.

child_profile: 20 months old, not yet playing with toys in a simple way, like pushing a toy car (most children do by 18 months).
activity_description: Give the child a toy to push or pull as they walk, such as a box tied to a short string. Clear a safe path and let them walk around the room or compound. Keep strings short and supervise.

child_profile: 20 months old; the caregiver would like support with sensory development; the child enjoys textures.
activity_description: Under close supervision, allow the child to pour water between safe containers in a shallow basin, exploring texture, sound, and cause-and-effect.

child_profile: 20 months old; the caregiver would like support with sensory development; the child enjoys textures.
activity_description: Fill an old bag with safe items like the ones you carry, such as an old phone, keys and family photos. Watch the child take them out and play with them just like you.
